commonPrompt: Use case: stylized-concept. Asset type: production 2D combat VFX overlay sprite sheet for AlarmQuest. Create exactly 16 chronological animation frames in a strict 4-column by 4-row, row-major sprite sheet. Every cell is a wide 361:160 combat viewport with the same fixed camera, scale, ground line, and central target point. Use CENTER_BREAKTHROUGH perspective, never side-scrolling motion: pressure, armored-force silhouettes, sparks, debris, dust, and perspective streaks converge toward the vanishing point at x=50% and y=55%, pierce straight through it toward the viewer, and then expand naturally past the viewport edges. This revision must solve insufficient screen coverage without scaling or stretching a single object. During F06-F12, build coverage from multiple physically distinct depth layers: a sharp central leading point, near-field pressure planes, curved shock rims, large foreground fragments, ground dust, and radial wakes. At F08-F10, the combined VFX must occupy at least 90% of the frame width and 82% of the frame height, with some foreground fragments or shock layers intentionally cropped by all four viewport edges. Preserve the natural local proportions and thickness of every wedge, rim, shard, and pressure front; achieve the wide composition by perspective placement and overlapping depth layers, never by horizontal scaling, smearing, mirroring, or flattening. Maximum impact density and screen coverage take priority across the center; no clean channel is required for skill labels or damage numbers. Visual effect only: no warrior body and no enemy body. Detailed premium Korean fantasy action-RPG VFX, hand-painted high-resolution 2D rendering, smooth tonal shading, crisp silhouettes, rich material detail, controlled bloom, and clean alpha. Frame choreography: F01 nearly transparent distant pressure; F02-F03 perspective lines and small depth layers gather; F04-F05 the leading core and separate mid-depth planes accelerate; F06-F07 near-field layers grow and begin reaching the viewport edges; F08 main center contact at full-screen coverage; F09 peak head-on breakthrough with the strongest depth expansion; F10-F12 large foreground fragments, curved shock rims, dust, and speed wakes rush from center past the outer edges; F13-F14 a broad but proportionally natural central tunnel and layered afterimages remain; F15-F16 clean fade to transparent. Each frame must be distinct yet continuous, with no camera pan, no camera rotation, and no loop reset. Transparent RGBA background. F01 and F16 must be mostly transparent. Do not render grid guides, frame labels, captions, or borders.
